candidates.expected_evidence: NASA astronauts practice team-building skills and exercises before their mission

Earth-based training in both high- and low-pressure environments prior to missions helps astronauts know what to expect in altered pressure situations, including when they might be at risk for decompression sickness.

Astronauts undergo routine bone scans before and after spaceflight to help researchers keep track of bone density changes, as well as the degree to which resistive exercise is helping to keep bones strong in microgravity.
limitations: The before/after scan timing describes bone scans, not an exercise schedule.

candidates.expected_evidence: People who plan to fly in high-altitude military aircraft breathe high levels of oxygen before the flight – much like astronauts do before a spacewalk – to help avoid decompression sickness.
limitations: The source compares military flight and astronaut practices; no oxygen concentration, duration or administration authorization is supplied.

candidates.expected_evidence: All astronauts perform exercise during their mission to counteract losses in bone density, muscle strength, and heart and blood vessel performance.
astronauts on the International Space Station perform resistance training and aerobic exercises for 1.5 hours per day to maintain their fitness and protect against muscle and bone loss
limitations: The duration and frequency describe the cited practice; they are not an individualized prescription.

candidates.expected_evidence: NASA encourages astronauts to explore self-care options including keeping a regular journal. In addition, research suggests growing fresh vegetables in space may provide therapeutic benefits by providing a tangible reminder of life back on Earth.

fields.indication: NASA encourages astronauts to explore self-care options including keeping a regular journal.

limitations: The source describes general self-care, not treatment of an anxiety disorder. The unreviewed condition association requires separate review. The investigational vegetable-growing statement is not promoted into a candidate.

candidates.expected_evidence: NASA astronauts train, on average, 300 hours in simulators before launch to help familiarize themselves with space vehicles and systems.
limitations: This is a reported prelaunch training average, not a required duration or an in-mission clinical action.

candidates.expected_evidence: light-emitting diodes, or LEDs, simulate Earth’s light-dark cycle to help astronauts sleep better
limitations: No lighting intensity, exposure time, spectrum or individualized schedule is documented in this excerpt.
